title: Hello service
tagline: A zokor service.
text:
A zokor service. Run it from the repository root: make example examples/hello/main.sl # examples/hello/main.sl Copy // A zokor service. // // Read the "the service" section below: that is the whole API, and it // ends at `listen_and_serve`. The section after that is a client, not a // server: it makes the same requests a curl would, over a real socket, // so this file demonstrates the service by running it rather than by // describing it. import "http" ; import "httpc" ; import "time" ; import "../../zokor" as zokor; // ---------------------------------------------------------------- // // the service // // ---------------------------------------------------------------- // gc struct App { name: str , requests: int , token: str , } fn home (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response { return zokor. text ( 200 , "hello from " + c.state.name); } fn search (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response { return zokor. text ( 200 , "q=" + c. query ( "q" ) + " page=" + to_str (c. query_int ( "page" , 1 ))); } fn show_org (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response { let _who = c. local ( "user_id" ); // put there by require_token if c. param ( "id" ) != "7" { return zokor. respond_with (c.errors, "org.not_found" , "no such organisation '" + c. param ( "id" ) + "'" , c.request_id); } return zokor. ok_json ( "{"org":"7"}" ); } // A DTO: a declared shape. `zokor.dto` fills it (slang's own // json.decode underneath), a missing field is an error rather than a // silent zero, and the field it names is already in the envelope. gc struct CreateOrg { name: str , plan: str , seats: i32 , website: opt [ str ], } fn create_org (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response { // the wire is camelCase, the struct is snake_case: no tags needed, // and a decode failure is already the response to return let r: result [CreateOrg, http.Response] = zokor. dto (c); guard let dto = r else let resp = err_of (r) { return resp; } // types are checked by the decoder; VALUES are checked here, and // every problem is reported at once let v = zokor. checker (); if len (dto.name) == 0 { v. note ( "name" , "must not be empty" ); } if dto.seats < 1 || dto.seats > 500 { v. note ( "seats" , "must be between 1 and 500" ); } if dto.plan != "free" && dto.plan != "pro" { v. note ( "plan" , "must be one of: free, pro" ); } if v. failed () { return zokor. respond_fields (c.errors, "validation_failed" , v.fields, c.request_id); } let body = zokor. jobj () . set_str ( "id" , "org_7" ) . set_str ( "name" , dto.name) . set_str ( "plan" , dto.plan) . set_int ( "seats" , dto.seats as int ) . set_opt_str ( "website" , dto.website); return zokor. created (zokor. camel_keys (body. render ()), "/orgs/org_7" ); } // A shape nobody declared: a webhook whose fields belong to somebody // else. `json_body` walks it without a struct. fn webhook (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response { let r = c. json_body (); guard let body = r else let e = err_of (r) { return zokor. respond_with (c.errors, e.code, e.detail, c.request_id); } let event = body. get ( "type" ). str_or ( "unknown" ); let city = body. path ( "data.customer.address.city" ). str_or ( "nowhere" ); let first_item = body. path ( "data.items.0.sku" ). str_or ( "none" ); return zokor. ok_json (zokor. jobj () . set_str ( "event" , event) . set_str ( "city" , city) . set_str ( "first_item" , first_item) . set_int ( "item_count" , body. path ( "data.items" ). size ()) . render ()); } fn asset (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response { return zokor. text ( 200 , "file " + c. param ( "rest" )); } // An upload: the rules say what is acceptable, and anything else comes // back as a registered failure rather than reaching this handler. fn upload_avatar (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response { let rules = zokor. with_max_file_bytes ( zokor. uploads_allowing ([ "image/png" , "image/jpeg" ]), 1048576 ); let r = c. upload (rules); guard let form = r else let e = err_of (r) { return zokor. respond_with (c.errors, e.code, e.detail, c.request_id); } guard let avatar = zokor. file (form, "avatar" ) else { return zokor. respond_with (c.errors, "validation_failed" , "no file was posted under 'avatar'" , c.request_id); } // avatar.filename is already safe to use as one path segment return zokor. ok_json ( "{"stored":"" + avatar.filename + "","type":"" + avatar.content_type + "","bytes":" + to_str ( len (avatar.data)) + ","title":"" + zokor. value (form, "title" ) + ""}" ); } // Middleware. A `before` may end the request, or resolve something and // hand it to the handler through the context; an `after` sees whatever // response came back, including one a before produced. // // Note what is NOT here: a list of public paths. This hook is attached // to a group, so it only ever runs for the routes inside it. fn require_token (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> opt [http.Response] { if c. bearer () != c.state.token { return some (zokor. respond (c.errors, "unauthorized" , c.request_id)); } // resolved once, at the edge, instead of in every handler c. set_local ( "user_id" , "u_1" ); return none ; } fn count (c: zokor.Ctx[App], r: http.Response) -> http.Response { c.state.requests = c.state.requests + 1 ; return zokor. with_header (r, "x-request-count" , to_str (c.state.requests)); } // Configuration is read once, here, and validated before anything runs. let cfg = zokor. load_config (); // base, profile, startup environment let app = App { name: zokor. str_or (cfg, "SERVICE_NAME" , "hello" ), requests: 0 , token: zokor. str_or (cfg, "API_TOKEN" , "s3cret" ) }; // new_router's own registry, carried onto every Ctx from here on -- // register the app's own codes on top of the built-ins it already has. let r = zokor. new_router (app); zokor. register (r.errors, "org.not_found" , 404 , "no such organisation" ); // public: no authentication r. get ( "/" , home); r. get ( "/search" , search); r. get ( "/files/*rest" , asset); // everything under /api needs a token, and says so once let api = r. group ( "/api" ); api. before (require_token); api. get ( "/orgs/:id" , show_org); api. post ( "/orgs" , create_org); api. post ( "/avatars" , upload_avatar); api. post ( "/webhooks/stripe" , webhook); // counted for every request, public or not r. after (count); // The whole server, from here on. `listen_and_serve` accepts and spawns // one task per connection; it returns when the process is asked to stop. // A real service calls it and nothing else -- the spawn here is only so // this file can also play the client below. // // It would also log every request (README, "Logging"). The client below // prints each exchange itself and the program ends the moment it is done, // so this demo turns the log off rather than interleave the two; a real // service keeps it. let sc = zokor. default_server_config (); sc.logger = zokor. no_logger (); spawn zokor. listen_and_serve_with (r, port (), sc); // ---------------------------------------------------------------- // // the demo: a real client, over a real socket // // // // Nothing below is part of zokor's API -- it is here so `make check` // // exercises the server end to end rather than describing it. // // ---------------------------------------------------------------- // // A function, not a top-level `let`: the client helpers below are // functions, and a top-level binding is local to the main task. fn port () -> int { return 18080 ; } fn base () -> str { return "http://127.0.0.1:" + to_str ( port ()); } fn deadline () -> until { return until_of (time. mono () + 5000000000 ); } fn send (rq: httpc.Request) -> httpc.Response { let c = httpc. new_client (); let r2 = httpc. client_send (c, rq, deadline ()); guard let resp = r2 else let e = err_of (r2) { println ( "request failed: " + e); exit ( 1 ); } return resp; } // Every request carries its own X-Request-Id, which the server reuses // (it is well-formed): the ids in the envelopes below are this one, so // the output is the same on every run instead of a fresh random id each. fn call (method: str , p: str , token: str , body: str , ctype: str ) -> httpc.Response { let rq = httpc. new_request (method, base () + p); rq.headers[ "x-request-id" ] = "example-req-1" ; if len (token) > 0 { rq.headers[ "authorization" ] = "Bearer " + token; } if len (body) > 0 { rq.headers[ "content-type" ] = ctype; rq.body = to_bytes (body); } return send (rq); } fn get (p: str ) -> httpc.Response { return call ( "GET" , p, "" , "" , "" ); } fn json_call (method: str , p: str , token: str , body: str ) -> httpc.Response { return call (method, p, token, body, "application/json" ); } fn show (label: str , resp: httpc.Response) { println (label + " -> " + to_str (resp.status) + " " + to_str (resp.body)); } // wait for the listener to be up before the first request fn wait_ready () { let i = 0 ; while i < 200 { let c = httpc. new_client (); let r2 = httpc. client_get (c, base () + "/" , deadline ()); guard let _ok = r2 else { time. sleep ( 10000000 ); i = i + 1 ; continue ; } return ; } println ( "server never came up" ); exit ( 1 ); } wait_ready (); println ( "routes:" ); for line in r. routes_list () { println ( " " + line); } println ( "" ); show ( "GET /" , get ( "/" )); show ( "GET /search?q=slang&page=2" , get ( "/search?q=slang&page=2" )); show ( "GET /api/orgs/7" , call ( "GET" , "/api/orgs/7" , "s3cret" , "" , "" )); show ( "GET /api/orgs/9" , call ( "GET" , "/api/orgs/9" , "s3cret" , "" , "" )); show ( "GET /api/orgs/7 (no token)" , get ( "/api/orgs/7" )); show ( "POST /api/orgs (empty body)" , call ( "POST" , "/api/orgs" , "s3cret" , "" , "" )); show ( "POST /api/orgs (bad values)" , json_call ( "POST" , "/api/orgs" , "s3cret" , "{"name":"","plan":"gold","seats":0}" )); show ( "POST /api/orgs (wrong type)" , json_call ( "POST" , "/api/orgs" , "s3cret" , "{"name":"acme","plan":"pro","seats":"many"}" )); show ( "POST /api/orgs (missing field)" , json_call ( "POST" , "/api/orgs" , "s3cret" , "{"name":"acme"}" )); show ( "POST /api/orgs" , json_call ( "POST" , "/api/orgs" , "s3cret" , "{"name":"acme","plan":"pro","seats":12,"website":"https://acme.test"}" )); show ( "POST /api/webhooks/stripe" , json_call ( "POST" , "/api/webhooks/stripe" , "s3cret" , "{"type":"invoice.paid","data":{"customer":{"address":{"city":"Lagos"}},"items":[{"sku":"A1"},{"sku":"B2"}]}}" )); let avatar = "--B
" + "Content-Disposition: form-data; name="title"

" + "My avatar
" + "--B
" + "Content-Disposition: form-data; name="avatar"; filename="../../etc/passwd.png"
" + "Content-Type: image/png

" + "PNGDATA
" + "--B--
" ; show ( "POST /avatars" , call ( "POST" , "/api/avatars" , "s3cret" , avatar, "multipart/form-data; boundary=B" )); let bad_avatar = "--B
" + "Content-Disposition: form-data; name="avatar"; filename="x.svg"
" + "Content-Type: image/svg+xml

" + "<svg/>
" + "--B--
" ; show ( "POST /avatars (svg)" , call ( "POST" , "/api/avatars" , "s3cret" , bad_avatar, "multipart/form-data; boundary=B" )); show ( "GET /files/a/b.txt" , get ( "/files/a/b.txt" )); show ( "HEAD /" , call ( "HEAD" , "/" , "" , "" , "" )); show ( "DELETE /api/orgs/7" , call ( "DELETE" , "/api/orgs/7" , "s3cret" , "" , "" )); show ( "BREW /" , call ( "BREW" , "/" , "" , "" , "" )); show ( "GET /nope" , call ( "GET" , "/nope" , "s3cret" , "" , "" )); println ( "" ); // one more than the calls above: wait_ready's probe is a request // like any other, and the `count` hook counts every one. println ( "requests served: " + to_str (app.requests));

title: Chat service
tagline: A chat service: the same room for WebSocket clients and socket.io clients, on one server.
text:
A chat service: the same room for WebSocket clients and socket.io clients, on one server. Run it from the repository root: make example-chat examples/chat/main.sl # examples/chat/main.sl Copy // A chat service: the same room for WebSocket clients and socket.io // clients, on one server. // // slangc examples/chat/main.sl --run the scripted demo below // slangc examples/chat/main.sl --run -- serve a real server on :8080 // // With `serve`, point a browser at it: // // const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8080/ws?name=ada", "chat"); // ws.onmessage = (m) => console.log(m.data); // ws.send("hello"); // // const socket = io("http://localhost:8080", { query: { name: "leo" } }); // socket.on("chat message", (m) => console.log(m)); // socket.emit("chat message", "hi", (reply) => console.log(reply)); // // Read "the service": that is everything a real one writes. The demo after // it is a stand-in browser -- real connections to a real server on a free // port -- so `make example-chat` shows the exchange without one. import "http" ; import "proc" ; import "time" ; import "../../zokor" as zokor; // ---------------------------------------------------------------- // // the service // // ---------------------------------------------------------------- // gc struct App { name: str , // everyone in the chat, WebSocket and socket.io alike hub: zokor.Hub, history: [ str ], lock: mutex , } fn remember (app: App, line: str ) { mutex_lock (app.lock); push (app.history, line); mutex_unlock (app.lock); } // The handshake, for both kinds of client. Every `before` has run by now // (an auth hook would have set c.local("user")); this one only wants a name. fn arrive (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response { let name = c. query ( "name" ); if name == "" { return zokor. respond_with (c.errors, "unauthorized" , "say who you are: ?name=" , c.request_id); } let s = c. socket (); s. set_local ( "name" , name); c.state.hub. join_room (s, "chat" ); return c. accept_ws (); } // WebSocket clients: every text message goes to the room. fn on_text (app: App, s: zokor.Socket, m: zokor.Message) { if m.kind != zokor.Incoming.Text { s. send_text ( "only text, please" ); return ; } if m.text == "/history" { mutex_lock (app.lock); let h = join_lines (app.history); mutex_unlock (app.lock); s. send_text (h); return ; } let line = s. local ( "name" ) + ": " + m.text; remember (app, line); // to WebSocket clients as text, to socket.io clients as an event app.hub. to_room ( "chat" , line, s.id); app.hub. emit_to_room ( "chat" , "/" , "chat message" , zokor. jstr (line). render (), s.id); } fn on_ws_close (app: App, s: zokor.Socket, code: int , reason: str ) { remember (app, s. local ( "name" ) + " left (" + to_str (code) + ")" ); } // socket.io clients. fn on_event (app: App, s: zokor.Socket, e: zokor.SioEvent) { if e.kind != zokor.SioKind.Event { return ; } if e.name == "chat message" { remember (app, s. local ( "name" ) + " said " + e.args_json); app.hub. emit_to_room ( "chat" , e.namespace, "chat message" , e.args_json, s.id); let said = "" ; let pr = zokor. parse (e.args_json); if let args = pr { said = args. at ( 0 ). str_or ( "" ); } app.hub. to_room ( "chat" , s. local ( "name" ) + ": " + said, s.id); if e.ack >= 0 { // the client used socket.emit(..., callback) s. ack (e.namespace, e.ack, "["delivered"]" ); } return ; } s. emit (e.namespace, "error" , ""unknown event: " + e.name + """ ); } fn on_sio_leave (app: App, s: zokor.Socket, ns: str , why: str ) { remember (app, s. local ( "name" ) + " left " + ns + " (" + why + ")" ); } fn chat_router (app: App) -> zokor.Router[App] { let r = zokor. new_router (app); r. websocket ( "/ws" , arrive, zokor. ws_route (zokor. ws_allowing ([ "chat" ]), on_text). on_close (on_ws_close)); r. socketio ( "/socket.io/" , arrive, zokor. sio_route (on_event). on_disconnect (on_sio_leave)); return r; } fn join_lines (xs: [ str ]) -> str { let out = "" ; let i = 0 ; while i < len (xs) { if i > 0 { out = out + " | " ; } out = out + xs[i]; i = i + 1 ; } return out; } fn new_app () -> App { return App { name: "zokor chat" , hub: zokor. new_hub (), history: [], lock: make_mutex () }; } // ---------------------------------------------------------------- // // the demo: a stand-in browser, printed // // // // Real connections to the server above. Nothing below is part of // // zokor's API: a browser does all of this for you. // // ---------------------------------------------------------------- // import "../../zokor/internal/ws" as frames; fn soon () -> until { return until_of (time. mono () + 2000000000 ); } // A client's frames are masked, which the server requires. fn client_frame (op: int , payload: bytes ) -> bytes { let n = len (payload); let head: bytes = b ".." ; head[ 0 ] = 128 | op; head[ 1 ] = 128 | n; let key = b "\x2a\x07\x63\x01" ; let body = b "" ; let one: bytes = b "." ; let i = 0 ; while i < n { one[ 0 ] = payload[i] ^ key[i % 4 ]; body = body + one; i = i + 1 ; } return head + key + body; } fn says (c: & mut link , s: str ) { let _s = c. send_bytes ( client_frame ( 1 , to_bytes (s)), soon ()); } fn bye (c: & mut link ) { let b: bytes = b ".." ; b[ 0 ] = 3 ; b[ 1 ] = 232 ; let _s = c. send_bytes ( client_frame ( 8 , b), soon ()); } // Sends the upgrade request and returns the status line; whatever came // after the response head is kept in `got`. gc struct Inbox { got: bytes , } fn open (c: & mut link , path: str , box: Inbox) -> str { let req = "GET " + path + " HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Upgrade: websocket
" + "Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
" + "Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
" + "Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: chat

" ; let _s = c. send_bytes ( to_bytes (req), soon ()); let a = arena_new ( 4096 ); let w = a. wire ( 4096 ); let got = b "" ; while true { let rr = c. recv (w, soon ()); guard let n = rr else { return "no answer" ; } if n == 0 { return "closed" ; } got = got + to_bytes (w[ 0..n ]); let i = 0 ; while i + 3 < len (got) { if got[i] == 13 && got[i + 1 ] == 10 && got[i + 2 ] == 13 && got[i + 3 ] == 10 { box.got = got[i + 4..len (got)]; let j = 0 ; while got[j] != 13 { j = j + 1 ; } return to_str (got[ 0..j ]); } i = i + 1 ; } } return "no answer" ; } // The next frame from the server, printed as a browser would see it. fn hears (label: str , c: & mut link , box: Inbox) { let a = arena_new ( 4096 ); let w = a. wire ( 4096 ); while true { let dr = frames. decode (box.got, 0 , 1048576 , false ); guard let d = dr else { println (label + " <- (undecodable)" ); return ; } if d.kind == frames.Decoded.Frame { let f = d.frame; box.got = box.got[f.size.. len (box.got)]; if f.op == frames.Op.Text { println (label + " <- " + to_str (f.payload)); } else if f.op == frames.Op.Close { let cr = frames. decode_close (f.payload); if let body = cr { println (label + " <- close " + to_str (body.code) + " " + body.reason); } else { println (label + " <- close" ); } } else { println (label + " <- frame " + to_str (frames. code_of (f.op))); } return ; } let rr = c. recv (w, soon ()); guard let n = rr else { println (label + " <- (nothing)" ); return ; } if n == 0 { println (label + " <- (connection closed)" ); return ; } box.got = box.got + to_bytes (w[ 0..n ]); } } fn serve_all (ln: link , r: zokor.Router[App]) { let sc = zokor. default_server_config (); sc.logger = zokor. no_logger (); let mut_ln = ln; while true { let ar = mut_ln. accept ( until_never ()); guard let c = ar else { return ; } spawn zokor. serve_conn (r, c, sc); } } // Waits until the server has finished with a client that left, so the // history printed at the end is complete. fn settle (app: App, lines: int ) { let waited = 0 ; while waited < 200 { mutex_lock (app.lock); let n = len (app.history); mutex_unlock (app.lock); if n >= lines { return ; } time. sleep ( 10000000 ); waited = waited + 1 ; } } fn demo () { let app = new_app (); let r = chat_router (app); let lr = link_listen ( 0 ); guard let ln = lr else { panic ( "cannot listen" ); } let port = ln. port (); spawn serve_all (ln, r); println ( "websocket:" ); let ada = link_dial ( "127.0.0.1" , port, soon ()) ?? panic_link (); let ab = Inbox { got: b "" }; println ( " ada handshake -> " + open (& mut ada, "/ws?name=ada" , ab)); let bo = link_dial ( "127.0.0.1" , port, soon ()) ?? panic_link (); let bb = Inbox { got: b "" }; println ( " bo handshake -> " + open (& mut bo, "/ws?name=bo" , bb)); let anon = link_dial ( "127.0.0.1" , port, soon ()) ?? panic_link (); let nb = Inbox { got: b "" }; println ( " anon handshake -> " + open (& mut anon, "/ws" , nb)); says (& mut ada, "hello" ); hears ( " bo " , & mut bo, bb); says (& mut bo, "hi ada" ); hears ( " ada " , & mut ada, ab); println ( "" ); println ( "socket.io:" ); let leo = link_dial ( "127.0.0.1" , port, soon ()) ?? panic_link (); let lb = Inbox { got: b "" }; println ( " leo handshake -> " + open (& mut leo, "/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket&name=leo" , lb)); // the session id is random; the rest of the open packet is not let a = arena_new ( 4096 ); let w = a. wire ( 4096 ); let opened = false ; while !opened { let dr = frames. decode (lb.got, 0 , 1048576 , false ); guard let d = dr else { break ; } if d.kind == frames.Decoded.Frame { let f = d.frame; lb.got = lb.got[f.size.. len (lb.got)]; let text = to_str (f.payload); let at = 0 ; let tb = to_bytes (text); while at < len (tb) && tb[at] != 44 { at = at + 1 ; } println ( " leo <- 0{"sid":"..."" + to_str (tb[at.. len (tb)])); opened = true ; } else { let rr = a_recv (& mut leo, w); lb.got = lb.got + rr; } } says (& mut leo, "40" ); let _ok = skip_one (& mut leo, lb); println ( " leo -> 40 (connected to /)" ); says (& mut leo, "421["chat message","hi from socket.io"]" ); hears ( " ada " , & mut ada, ab); hears ( " bo " , & mut bo, bb); hears ( " leo " , & mut leo, lb); says (& mut ada, "and back" ); hears ( " bo " , & mut bo, bb); hears ( " leo " , & mut leo, lb); says (& mut leo, "42["whatever"]" ); hears ( " leo " , & mut leo, lb); println ( "" ); println ( "leaving:" ); bye (& mut ada); hears ( " ada " , & mut ada, ab); settle (app, 5 ); says (& mut leo, "41" ); settle (app, 6 ); says (& mut bo, "/history" ); hears ( " bo " , & mut bo, bb); } fn a_recv (c: & mut link , w: wire ) -> bytes { let rr = c. recv (w, soon ()); guard let n = rr else { return b "" ; } return to_bytes (w[ 0..n ]); } // The CONNECT answer carries the random session id too: read past it. fn skip_one (c: & mut link , box: Inbox) -> bool { let a = arena_new ( 4096 ); let w = a. wire ( 4096 ); while true { let dr = frames. decode (box.got, 0 , 1048576 , false ); guard let d = dr else { return false ; } if d.kind == frames.Decoded.Frame { box.got = box.got[d.frame.size.. len (box.got)]; return true ; } let rr = c. recv (w, soon ()); guard let n = rr else { return false ; } if n == 0 { return false ; } box.got = box.got + to_bytes (w[ 0..n ]); } return false ; } fn panic_link () -> link { panic ( "cannot connect" ); } let args = proc. args (); if len (args) > 1 && args[ len (args) - 1 ] == "serve" { let r = chat_router ( new_app ()); let sr = zokor. listen_and_serve (r, 8080 ); guard let _ok = sr else let e = err_of (sr) { println (e); exit ( 1 ); } } else { demo (); }

title: Ports and fakes
tagline: Ports and fakes
text: The example is built from the source files below, with tests beside each package. Run it from the repository root: make example-ports examples/ports/src/application/inventory/ports.sl # examples/ports/src/application/inventory/ports.sl Copy import "../../domain/inventory" as stock; // C is explicit adapter state: function fields never capture credentials or globals. pub gc struct StockPort[C] { context: C, lookup: fn (C, str , str ) -> result [ opt [stock.Stock], str ], } examples/ports/src/application/inventory/service.sl # examples/ports/src/application/inventory/service.sl Copy import "../../domain/inventory" as stock; import "strings" ; pub gc struct Service[C] { port: StockPort[C] } pub fn new_service[C](port: StockPort[C]) -> Service[C] { return Service[C] { port: port }; } // Tenant identity is resolved at the edge and passed through every port call. pub fn find[C](service: Service[C], tenant_id: str , sku: str ) -> result [ opt [stock.Stock], str ] { let checked = stock. key (tenant_id, sku); guard let _key = checked else let e = err_of (checked) { return err (e); } let lookup = service.port.lookup; let loaded = lookup (service.port.context, tenant_id, sku); guard let maybe = loaded else let e = err_of (loaded) { return err (e); } if let row = maybe { if row.tenant_id != tenant_id || row.sku != sku { return err ( "adapter returned a different tenant_id or sku" ); } if row.available < 0 { return err ( "adapter returned a negative available count" ); } } return ok (maybe); } // Share the domain rule with the HTTP edge without importing adapters. pub fn valid_sku (sku: str ) -> bool { return stock. identifier (sku); } examples/ports/src/domain/inventory/stock.sl # examples/ports/src/domain/inventory/stock.sl Copy import "strings" ; pub struct Stock { tenant_id: str , sku: str , available: int } pub fn identifier (value: str ) -> bool { if len (value) < 1 || len (value) > 64 { return false ; } for ch in to_bytes (value) { if !((ch >= 65 && ch <= 90 ) || (ch >= 97 && ch <= 122 ) || (ch >= 48 && ch <= 57 ) || ch == 45 || ch == 95 ) { return false ; } } return true ; } // The separator cannot occur in either identifier: tenant keys stay distinct. pub fn key (tenant_id: str , sku: str ) -> result [ str , str ] { let problems: [ str ] = []; if ! identifier (tenant_id) { push (problems, "tenant_id must contain 1..64 ASCII letters, digits, - or _" ); } if ! identifier (sku) { push (problems, "sku must contain 1..64 ASCII letters, digits, - or _" ); } if len (problems) > 0 { return err (strings. join (problems, "; " )); } return ok (tenant_id + ":" + sku); } pub fn new_stock (tenant_id: str , sku: str , available: int ) -> result [Stock, str ] { let problems: [ str ] = []; let checked = key (tenant_id, sku); if let _key = checked {} else let e = err_of (checked) { push (problems, e); } if available < 0 { push (problems, "available must be nonnegative" ); } if len (problems) > 0 { return err (strings. join (problems, "; " )); } return ok (Stock { tenant_id: tenant_id, sku: sku, available: available }); } examples/ports/src/infrastructure/memory/client.sl # examples/ports/src/infrastructure/memory/client.sl Copy import "../../application/inventory" as inventory; import "../../domain/inventory" as stock; import "strings" ; // Seed once at startup; immutable afterwards, so readers do not need a lock. pub gc struct Store { stocks: map [ str ]stock.Stock } pub fn new_store (rows: [stock.Stock]) -> result [Store, str ] { let values: map [ str ]stock.Stock = {}; let problems: [ str ] = []; let i = 0 ; for row in rows { let made = stock. new_stock (row.tenant_id, row.sku, row.available); guard let checked = made else let e = err_of (made) { push (problems, "rows[" + to_str (i) + "]: " + e); i += 1 ; continue ; } let key = stock. key (checked.tenant_id, checked.sku) ?? "" ; if has (values, key) { push (problems, "rows[" + to_str (i) + "]: duplicate tenant_id and sku" ); } else { values[key] = checked; } i += 1 ; } if len (problems) > 0 { return err (strings. join (problems, "; " )); } return ok (Store { stocks: values }); } pub fn lookup (ctx: Store, tenant_id: str , sku: str ) -> result [ opt [stock.Stock], str ] { let checked = stock. key (tenant_id, sku); guard let key = checked else let e = err_of (checked) { return err (e); } if ! has (ctx.stocks, key) { let absent: opt [stock.Stock] = none ; return ok (absent); } return ok ( some (ctx.stocks[key])); } pub fn new_stock_port (ctx: Store) -> inventory.StockPort[Store] { return inventory.StockPort[Store] { context: ctx, lookup: lookup }; } examples/ports/src/interfaces/web/router.sl # examples/ports/src/interfaces/web/router.sl Copy import "../../../../../zokor" as zokor; import "../../application/inventory" as inventory; import "http" ; import "json" ; pub fn register_errors (errors: zokor.Registry) { zokor. register (errors, "inventory.not_found" , 404 , "stock not found" ); zokor. register (errors, "inventory.unavailable" , 503 , "inventory is unavailable" ); } // The route wrapper resolves authentication and passes explicit values here. pub fn show[C](service: inventory.Service[C], tenant_id: str , sku: str , errors: zokor.Registry, request_id: str ) -> http.Response { if !inventory. valid_sku (sku) { return zokor. respond_fields (errors, "validation_failed" , [zokor. field ( "sku" , "must contain 1..64 ASCII letters, digits, - or _" )], request_id); } let loaded = inventory. find (service, tenant_id, sku); guard let maybe = loaded else { return zokor. respond (errors, "inventory.unavailable" , request_id); } guard let row = maybe else { return zokor. respond (errors, "inventory.not_found" , request_id); } return zokor. ok_json (json. encode (row)); } examples/ports/src/main.sl # examples/ports/src/main.sl Copy // Startup wiring is the only package that knows the concrete adapter. import "application/inventory" as inventory; import "domain/inventory" as stock; import "infrastructure/memory" as memory; import "interfaces/web" as rest; import "../../../zokor" as zokor; import "http" ; gc struct App { inventory: inventory.Service[memory.Store], tokens: zokor.TokenStore } fn require_tenant (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> opt [http.Response] { guard let tenant_id = zokor. bearer_subject (c, c.state.tokens) else { return some (zokor. respond (c.errors, "unauthorized" , c.request_id)); } c. set_local ( "tenant_id" , tenant_id); return none ; } fn show_stock (c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response { return rest. show (c.state.inventory, c. local ( "tenant_id" ), c. param ( "sku" ), c.errors, c.request_id); } fn main () { let cfg = zokor. load_config (); let count = zokor. int_or (cfg, "EXAMPLE_STOCK" , 7 ); let checked = zokor. check (cfg); guard let _config = checked else let e = err_of (checked) { println (e); exit ( 1 ); } let made = stock. new_stock ( "tenant_a" , "pen" , count); guard let row = made else let e = err_of (made) { println (e); exit ( 1 ); } let seeded = memory. new_store ([row]); guard let adapter = seeded else let e = err_of (seeded) { println (e); exit ( 1 ); } let service = inventory. new_service (memory. new_stock_port (adapter)); let tokens = zokor. new_token_store ( 0 ); let issued = tokens. issue ( "tenant_a" ); guard let token = issued else { println ( "token issue failed" ); exit ( 1 ); } let router = zokor. new_router (App { inventory: service, tokens: tokens }); rest. register_errors (router.errors); router. before (require_tenant); router. get ( "/stock/:sku" , show_stock);
